sources.title: Design request of 2026-09-23, without the onboarding SOP
sources.summary: The request asked to turn an onboarding SOP into actions, approvals and exception paths and stated that some required context is unavailable. No SOP file, extract or quotation was supplied and the working directory was empty. The only requirements traceable to this source are: the process is employee onboarding, it must produce actions, it must contain approvals, and it must contain exception paths. Everything else in this design is a proposal from generic onboarding practice and carries no source authority.

sections.title: The design must contain exception paths
Assumed baseline: not stated in any supplied source

sources.title: Onboarding SOP (named in the request, not supplied)
sources.summary: The document the request refers to. It was not supplied and no part of it was read. No element of this design is derived from it, and nothing in this manifest cites it. It must be supplied and reconciled against this design before packaging (decision D1).

groups.name: Human Resources
groups.purpose: Opens the onboarding case, collects the employee's documents, prepares the contract and the payroll registration, decides on the start readiness and runs the day-one induction. Proposed actor: no supplied source names it.

flags.detail: No supplied source names the team that owns onboarding. The key, the name and the responsibilities are proposals; decision D3 names the real owner.

groups.name: IT
groups.purpose: Creates the approved accounts and system access and prepares the workstation and equipment. Proposed actor: no supplied source names it.

flags.detail: No supplied source names the team that provisions access and equipment. Decision D3 names the real owner.
IT grants the access that the hiring manager approves in approve_plan. Keep the approval and the provisioning in different groups; decision D5 asks whether privileged access needs a second approver.

groups.name: Hiring Managers
groups.purpose: Fallback owner for the actions the hiring manager of the case performs: approving the onboarding plan and the access list, introducing the employee to the team and deciding on the end of the onboarding period. Used only where the per-case owner in the hiring_manager field cannot be applied.

flags.detail: The hiring manager is per case, not a standing team. This role group exists because Provia cannot assign from a case field; decision D6 confirms who holds it.

workflows.name: Employee onboarding

grants.reason: Proposed, not evidenced: Human Resources owns the onboarding design and opens every case. edit is cumulative, so it also carries create_incident. Confirm in decision D4 before applying.

access.note: Sensitivity is a proposal, not a reading of the source: no supplied document uses the words that would set it. The case carries identity documents, a contract and a payroll registration, so decision D7 asks whether the workflow should be restricted. IT and the hiring managers receive no grant: they see the cases that carry their own actions. Nobody beyond Human Resources and the organization administrators can see every case under the proposal above.

triggers.label: Intake from the recruiting handover (proposed, not designed)

unresolvedEntityTypes.name: Employee
unresolvedEntityTypes.detail: The onboarding case is about a person who will also be a reusable record (payroll, equipment, later processes). No entity type registry was supplied, so no key is invented here; provia-information-model must decide whether an Employee entity type exists and bind it.

actions.name: Register the confirmed hire and open the onboarding case
evidence: Signed offer or hire confirmation attached to the case
employee_name, role_title, department, start_date and hiring_manager filled

folded.summary: Confirm with the recruiting owner that the offer was accepted (hand-off, not a separate unit of work)
Tell the hiring manager that the case is open so the plan and access list can be prepared

actions.name: Collect and check the new employee's documents
evidence: Each collected document attached to the case
Comment mapping each attachment to the list item it satisfies and naming anything outstanding

folded.summary: Send the document list to the new employee (sub-step of the collection task)

actions.name: Decide on the onboarding plan and the access list
evidence: Approved onboarding plan and access list attached to the case
Comment with the reason on a return or a cancellation

actions.name: Prepare the employment contract and the payroll registration
evidence: Signed employment contract attached to the case
Payroll registration confirmation attached to the case

folded.summary: Send the contract for signature by the signatories and the employee (sub-step)
Register the employee for the benefits the role carries; decision D8 asks whether payroll and benefits belong to this process at all

actions.name: Create the accounts and the system access
evidence: Comment listing each system, the account created and the permission level granted
Delivery method of the first-access credentials recorded

folded.summary: Prepare first-access credentials for in-person delivery on day one (sub-step)

actions.name: Prepare the workstation and the equipment
evidence: Comment listing the prepared equipment with asset identifiers
Unsigned handover record attached to the case

actions.name: Decide whether the start proceeds on the planned date
evidence: Comment recording the four-item readiness check
Updated start_date when the start is postponed

folded.summary: Verify documents, contract, access and equipment before day one (the readiness checklist is the method of this decision, not four separate actions)

actions.name: Run the day-one induction
evidence: Signed equipment handover record attached to the case
Comment confirming the induction was held and the employee signed in successfully

folded.summary: Hand over the equipment and the first-access credentials, and introduce the employee to the hiring manager (hand-offs inside the induction)

actions.name: Introduce the new employee and agree the role plan
evidence: Comment with the agreed objectives for the onboarding period and the first point of contact
Short record of each follow-up conversation held

folded.summary: Name the colleague who is the employee's first point of contact (sub-step)

actions.name: Decide on the end of the onboarding period
evidence: Comment with the closing assessment against the agreed objectives

folded.summary: Hold the closing conversation with the employee (sub-step of the decision)

setupNotes: No onboarding SOP was supplied. This workflow is a proposal built on a declared assumed baseline; do not publish it before the actual SOP is supplied and reconciled against it (decision D1).
No deadline is set on any action because no service level was supplied. Every due is unset by design, not by omission (decision D2).

approve_plan, introduce_to_team and decide_period_end are owned per case by the user in the hiring_manager field. Provia cannot assign from a case field: configure the Hiring Managers group as the assignee and set the owner manually per case, or accept the fallback (decision D6).
The intake form trigger is recorded as a proposal only. A form trigger cannot be authored in the portable YAML; it must be created in Provia and specified by provia-form-designer (decision D9).
Group ids do not exist yet. The YAML carries no assignee for any action and the access grant is written by group name; both need real destination references before import.

A provia-implementer MCP server was offered in the design session but the org_get_context call was not permitted, so the tenant was never read. The design is disconnected: no group, user, entity type or workflow was read from or written to Provia, and every group key here is a proposal rather than a tenant reference.

decisions.question: Which document is the actual onboarding SOP, and where does this proposed design differ from it? Nothing here was derived from a customer document.

What service level applies to each action: document collection, contract and payroll, access provisioning, equipment, the readiness decision and the length of the onboarding period? No due was invented.
Which real teams own the work proposed here as Human Resources and IT, and what are their names in the tenant? The group keys and names are placeholders.

Who opens an onboarding case: Human Resources only, as proposed, or may a hiring manager open one directly? The answer decides whether a second create_incident grant or a manual-start allowlist is needed.
Does the hiring manager alone approve the access list, or does privileged or system-administrator access need a second approver? No threshold or approval rule was supplied and none was invented.

Provia cannot assign an action from a case field. For approve_plan, introduce_to_team and decide_period_end, should the assignee be set manually per case from hiring_manager, or should the Hiring Managers group hold them?

Should this workflow be restricted rather than internal? The case carries identity documents, an employment contract and a payroll registration. No supplied document uses the words that would settle it.
Are payroll and benefits registration part of onboarding, as folded into prepare_contract here, or a separate process with its own owner?
Is the case opened manually by Human Resources, as designed, or from an intake form handed over by recruiting? A form trigger is not authorable in the portable YAML and must be configured in Provia.

Does ending the onboarding period without completing it belong in this workflow at all? decide_period_end closes the case and leaves any employment consequence outside; confirm that a separate process handles it.

Country, jurisdiction and response language were not supplied. Angola, Africa/Luanda and AOA are recorded as a provisional starting context and the design is written in English; confirm or correct before publication.
